summary: A higher abstraction layer can multiply leverage, but it can also hide defects, create metric gaming and separate operators from the system they remain accountable for.

points.text: Small teams or one-off tasks may have no coordination bottleneck. Adding task states, dashboards and pipeline policy can cost more than working directly at the code layer.

Observable proxies become targets. Agents and operators can optimize completion counts or queue age while quality, maintainability and user value decline; pair flow measures with independent outcome checks and sampled audits.

Validation errors can be correlated across agents because they share a model, prompt, fixture or review policy. More passing runs do not create independent evidence unless the checks exercise genuinely different failure modes.

Frequent movement between aggregate management and raw implementation has its own context-switching cost. Use explicit descent triggers and compact evidence bundles instead of continuously hovering between layers.
